title: StreamMuxer connector and committable-ack contract ergonomics for Python SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Customers building streaming chat UIs need predictable semantics for partial responses, retries, and durable consumer progress. Current Python SDK patterns mix callback-based streaming, raw event crates, and ad-hoc checkpointing. This ticket defines a StreamMuxer connector and a committable-ack contract to make common workflows ergonomic: multiplexing multiple logical streams over a single network connection, explicit soft/committable ack semantics, and helpers for idempotent resume and backpressure-aware consumption.
background: We have many engineering tickets exploring resume hooks, checkpointing, and incremental iterators (see dependency list). Frontend teams keep reimplementing the same primitives: watermarking, heartbeat detection, patch-apply events, and merge/conflict semantics when reconnecting. This causes fragmentation, harder telemetry correlation, and repeated bugs in retries or duplicate UI inserts.
proposal: Introduce a StreamMuxer class in the Python SDK which exposes: 1) an async iterator per logical topic (conversation-id, ephemeral stream id); 2) a CommittableAck token object returned with each batch of events that exposes commit() and soft_ack() semantics; 3) built-in watermarking via monotonic sequence numbers and optional strong-idempotency tokens; 4) a small adapter layer to convert existing streaming payloads (SSE/HTTP/WS) into muxed events. Provide higher-level helpers: ResumableConversationConsumer, PatchApplier, and a StreamCheckpointStore abstraction used by customers or Redwood's dedicated rollout tests.
api_sketch:
from redwood.sdk.streaming import StreamMuxer

async with StreamMuxer.connect(url, api_key) as muxer:
    conv_iter = muxer.open_topic('conversation:123')  # async iterator of (events, ack_token)
    async for events, ack in conv_iter:
        apply_patch(events)
        if state_consistent():
            await ack.commit()  # durable commit persisted to checkpoint store
        else:
            await ack.soft_ack()  # makes progress but allows replay on reconnect

Ack token shape: CommittableAck.commit(checkpoint_meta: dict) -> awaitable; CommittableAck.soft_ack() -> awaitable; CommittableAck.id -> str (opaque id for telemetry)
tradeoffs: - Surface complexity vs ergonomics: StreamMuxer adds an abstraction layer that might hide raw events needed by low-level debugging. We mitigate this by providing a raw_topic() shim that yields the original wire events.\n- Strong committable semantics require a checkpoint store. For hosted customers we'll provide a managed checkpoint store; private deployments will default to a file-backed or KVS-backed implementation template.\n- Backpressure: multiplexing helps batching but can increase latencies for small streams; expose per-topic flow-control knobs and a global concurrency cap.
rollout_plan: 1) RFC and design doc (this ticket) -> 2) internal prototype and unit tests -> 3) land core StreamMuxer and CommittableAck in experimental module (feature flag on SDK) -> 4) integration test with console telemetry and a small beta group -> 5) documentation, examples, and stable release. Target landing in runtime-1.21 integration tests before SDK stable release.
acceptance_criteria: API sketch implemented with unit tests for commit/soft_ack semantics
ResumableConsumer demo notebook that recovers from process kill and replays to last committed checkpoint
Integration e2e test showing no duplicates when client retries after transient network failure
Documentation + examples added to SDK docs and examples repo
Feature flagged and toggled off by default for private customers until KVS integration covered
updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after ad-hoc sync with frontend team; initial API sketch drafted.
2026-03-11: Spike: prototyped CommittableAck as a dataclass wrapping checkpoint id + serializer; observed race when commit inflight and reconnect—added inflight-guard to ack implementation.

2026-03-12: Design review with Runtime and Console teams. Decided to add raw_topic() shim and to require opt-in managed checkpoint store for hosted Stable release. Mateo assigned to implement experimental module and tests. Linked PR and design doc.
